changeLog.summary: Increased Aditya-L1's satellite model size against the Sun, and fixed a camera-lerp bug where the Sun-to-Earth return transition took much longer than intended (this chat session, filesystem-only access)
changes: Added SAT_MODEL_SCALE_OVERRIDES in JourneyScene.tsx keyed by orbitType (currently just 'l1', which only Aditya-L1 uses) -- doubled its model scale from the shared SAT_MODEL_SCALE=1.3 baseline to 2.6, since that baseline was tuned against the much smaller Moon/Mars/leo/geo subjects and read as a barely-visible speck against SUN_RADIUS=18. OrbitingSatellite now reads SAT_MODEL_SCALE_OVERRIDES[orbitType] ?? SAT_MODEL_SCALE instead of the flat constant, so every other satellite/orbitType is untouched

Bug fix: CameraController's fast-vs-slow camera lerp-rate decision previously used a one-frame flag (prevMissionKindRef, tracking whether the LAST frame was a destination-body shot) to decide when to use the fast 0.12 catch-up rate vs the gentle 0.03 rate. That flag was overwritten at the bottom of the same useFrame call it was read in, so the fast rate only ever applied for the single frame the mission label changed -- the entire multi-hundred-frame return leg from the Sun (SUN_CAM_OFFSET ~170 units from CAMERA_SATELLITE) crawled back at the slow rate instead, roughly 4x longer than intended, matching the reported 'camera transition between the Sun and Earth rolls out twice as long' bug (same underlying issue also affected the Mars Orbiter Mission -> AstroSat return leg)

Fix: replaced the flag-based decision with a distance-based one -- computes camera.position.distanceTo(targetPos.current) every frame and uses the fast 0.12 rate whenever that distance exceeds a new DESTINATION_LERP_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD=20 world units, gentle 0.03 otherwise. This is symmetric in both directions (arriving at OR leaving any destination) and has no flag to expire early -- the fast rate stays active for as many consecutive frames as the camera is actually still far from its target. Removed prevMissionKindRef and the isDestinationMission/isLeavingDestination flags entirely, no longer needed

changeLog.summary: Ensured the site runs more smoothly: throttled React re-renders during scroll, gated shadow mapping and DPR by performanceMode (this chat session, filesystem-only access, fixes A1-A3 of fix.md)
changes: Wrote fix.md at the project root documenting a full performance review (Canvas/GL settings, lighting, textures, GLB loading, scroll/state architecture) with 6 prioritized findings (A1-A3 safe code-only, B1-B3 needing a decision on asset/behavior changes) before making any edits, per explicit instruction to confirm before adding anything.

A1 (JourneyProvider.tsx): the smoothing rAF loop previously called setProgress() on almost every animation frame (~60x/sec) while easing toward the raw scroll target, re-rendering JourneyOverlay's full JSX tree in lockstep with the WebGL frame loop on the same main thread. Added lastEmittedProgressRef, which now gates setProgress() so it only fires when progress rounded to 3 decimal places has actually changed, in both the smoothing-loop tick() and the instant-teleport setProgressDirect(). progressRef (read directly by the 3D scene in JourneyScene.tsx's useFrame) is completely unaffected and still updates every single frame.

A2 (SpaceEnvironment.tsx, Earth.tsx): the main directional light's 2048x2048 shadow map (castShadow) previously rendered every frame on every performanceMode tier, including 'low' -- the only mesh using it is Earth self-shadowing itself, whose day/night look is already produced by its own custom atmosphere terminator shader, so the real shadow map bought little visible benefit for its cost. castShadow on the light and castShadow/receiveShadow on Earth's mesh are now both gated to performanceMode !== 'low' (skipped entirely on 'low'), with shadow-mapSize additionally dropping from 2048x2048 to 1024x1024 on 'medium' -- 'high' keeps the original full-quality shadow untouched.

A3 (JourneyScene.tsx): the <Canvas> had no dpr cap at all, so a high-DPI phone (devicePixelRatio 3) rendered every pass at 9x the fragment cost of dpr 1, with usePerformanceMode's own device-capability detection never wired into pixel density anywhere. Added dpr={[1, performanceMode === 'high' ? 2 : 1]} to the Canvas -- 'high' tier still renders up to 2x, low/medium tiers are now capped at 1x.

Updated fix.md to mark A1-A3 as implemented (with a short 'Implemented as' note under each) and B1-B3 as still awaiting a go-ahead, so the file stays an accurate running record rather than a stale proposal.

Not verified visually in this session (filesystem-only access, no execution capability against this project) -- should be spot-checked once running: overall scroll smoothness (A1), that Earth/shadow visuals look correct across all three performanceMode tiers (A2), and that rendering still looks crisp at typical viewport sizes with the new dpr cap (A3).
B1 (texture re-encode), B2 (staged GLB preload), and B3 (remove unused lenis dependency) are intentionally NOT implemented -- explicitly deferred pending a separate decision, per fix.md.

The fast 0.12 lerp rate now also fires whenever isLeavingDestination is true (prevMissionKindRef.current === 'destination' && !isDestinationMission), so both directions of a long cross-body jump — into a destination AND back out of one — get the same brisk catch-up rate instead of only the outbound leg. Short in-scene moves (every other phase transition, plus leo<->geo) are unaffected and keep the original smooth 0.03 rate

changeLog.summary: Changed satellite GLB normalization to size by the spacecraft BUS only, excluding solar panels/arrays (this chat session)
changes: GLBModel (SatelliteModel.tsx) previously normalized every satellite GLB against its FULL model bounding box (bus + deployed solar panels/arrays), so satellites whose panels span wide (comms/nav types with two large flat arrays) had their BUS scaled down more than satellites with small or no panels (e.g. AstroSat's compact cylinder) — panel span was dominating the 'largest dimension' used for normalization, so spacecraft bodies read as visibly inconsistent sizes across missions even though the buses are what should look uniform (panels legitimately vary in span per real mission and are meant to)

Added a name-based isPanelLikeName() heuristic (matches 'panel'/'solar'/'array'/'wing'/'sap', case-insensitive substring — same pattern already used for RocketGLB.tsx's floor-plate filter) and now compute a BUS-ONLY THREE.Box3 by traversing every mesh in each cloned GLB scene graph and skipping ones whose name matches it; falls back to the full-model box if a GLB has no matching bus geometry (missing name metadata, or every mesh happens to match the heuristic)

Renamed NORMALIZED_MODEL_SIZE to NORMALIZED_BUS_SIZE (still 2.2 world units) to reflect what it now actually normalizes; centerOffset is now the bus box's center (not the full model's), so the model's local (0,0,0) pivot sits on the bus's own visual center rather than being skewed off-center by an asymmetric panel. The outer scale group still scales bus AND panels together as one rigid object, so panels stay correctly attached/proportioned to their bus — only the normalization TARGET changed from 'whole model's largest dimension' to 'bus's largest dimension'

Fixed MOON_CAM_OFFSET/MARS_CAM_OFFSET/SUN_CAM_OFFSET being sized only against the camera's vertical FOV: a PerspectiveCamera's horizontal FOV is narrower than vertical on any portrait/narrow-aspect viewport (halfWidthVisible = distance * aspect * tan(verticalFOV/2)), so the previous distances clipped each satellite's full orbit out of frame horizontally on phone-shaped canvases even though it stayed within vertical bounds. Recomputed each offset with a ~20% safety margin against the true orbit-bounding-radius at an assumed worst-case aspect (Moon d≈38, Mars d≈67, Sun/L1 d≈124 — L1's orbit is a true circle of radius SAT_ORBIT_L1_R=24, the largest of the three) (JourneyScene.tsx)

Fixed a camera-transition-lag symptom ("satellite not found on its planet", reported after the fixes above) where camera.lookAt() snapped to the destination body instantly every frame but camera.position only eased toward it at the same slow 0.03/frame rate used for every short in-scene move — closing the 40–190+ world-unit gap between Earth's LEO/GEO vantage and Moon/Mars/Sun's own vantage could take a couple of seconds, long enough to still be mid-transit when a lunar/mars/l1 mission's scroll segment began. First tried a faster 0.08/frame catch-up rate for these jumps specifically, then replaced that with a decisive fix once a follow-up screenshot showed Mars still transiently huge/cropped mid-transit: camera.position now SNAPS directly (camera.position.copy(), no easing at all) for lunar/mars/l1 missions, matching lookAt's own instant snap, so no transit path (and no bad intermediate frame on it) can exist at all. LEO/GEO keeps its original smooth 0.03 easing, since it never leaves the same near-Earth vantage for the whole rocket-launch cinematic (JourneyScene.tsx: CameraController, isDestinationMission)

Found and fixed the actual root cause of the satellite/orbit-ring being visibly displaced from its real Moon/Mars/Sun position (worse the later in the journey a mission fell — mild for Chandrayaan-1, severe for Aditya-L1, per user screenshots): SatelliteEvolution's outer group (anchored at EARTH_POS) is a single object that's never unmounted across the whole journey, and its idle-spin rotation.y accumulated during every leo/geo mission's screen time was NEVER reset. destCenter (the Moon/Mars/Sun offset) was positioned as a CHILD of that same group, so any leftover rotation swung the entire destination-body offset around EARTH_POS's Y axis by however much had built up by that point — worse the more leo/geo missions had played out before a given lunar/mars/l1 mission. An earlier pass in this session had already tried restricting the idle spin to only ADD to leo/geo (not stopping it from applying to lunar/mars/l1), which didn't address the pre-existing accumulated rotation and didn't fix the bug. Real fix: restructured the group nesting so destCenter can never sit inside a rotating group at all — added a new spinGroupRef wrapping only the orbit lines/tracking grid/satellite/particles, nested INSIDE the destCenter-positioned group rather than around it, so the idle spin still visually rotates leo/geo's own contents around Earth's local origin (harmless, since destCenter=[0,0,0] there) while the destination-body offset itself is now structurally immune to any amount of accumulated spin (JourneyScene.tsx: SatelliteEvolution, spinGroupRef)

Verified GLB model files for the affected missions (CHANDRAYAAN-2.glb etc.) exist on disk and are non-empty/non-corrupted, and independently re-verified the destCenter world-position math (EARTH_POS + MOON_LOCAL == MOON_POS, etc.) algebraically before concluding the bugs above were camera-transition and rotation-accumulation issues rather than a position-formula error

changeLog.summary: Fixed satellite model scale/origin normalization -- root cause of several bugs from a 20-item external bug report (mistakeprompt.md) that survived multiple earlier tuning passes (this chat session)
changes: Found and fixed the actual root cause behind persistent 'satellites too small / huge white circle rendering error / inconsistent scale between GLTF files' reports (mistakeprompt.md #4, #8, #9, #19), which earlier sessions had already tried to fix by wiring SAT_MODEL_SCALE into OrbitingSatellite's scale prop (see the 'satellite scale fix' changelog entry below) without success: SatelliteModel.tsx's own useFrame hover-animation was overwriting groupRef's ENTIRE scale every frame via `.setScalar(currentScale.current)`, where currentScale only ever tracked an absolute NORMAL_SCALE(1.0)/HOVER_SCALE(1.15) value -- completely discarding whatever `scale` prop the caller had passed in (SAT_MODEL_SCALE=0.22, hero-orbit 0.65, stowed/deployed payload 0.4, etc.), the instant the first frame ran. Every satellite instance was therefore always rendering at ~1.0x its raw model size regardless of the scale any caller specified, which is why lowering SAT_MODEL_SCALE in earlier sessions (0.35 -> 0.22) never visibly took effect. Fixed by computing the hover target as `scale * (hovered ? HOVER_SCALE : NORMAL_SCALE)` each frame instead of a bare absolute value, so the caller's scale prop is now a real multiplier again (SatelliteModel.tsx)

Added bounding-box-based normalization for all 23 real satellite GLB models (SatelliteModel.tsx: GLBModel): the 23 files come from different export pipelines with different native scales and origins, and were previously cloned and rendered exactly as authored with no normalization at all. GLBModel now computes each model's THREE.Box3 once, offsets the geometry by -center (so the bounding-box center -- not whatever arbitrary point the GLB used as its root origin -- sits at local (0,0,0), fixing mistakeprompt.md #10 'model origin/pivot points inconsistent'), then scales the whole thing so its largest dimension becomes a shared NORMALIZED_MODEL_SIZE=2.2 world units before the caller's own per-context scale prop is applied on top (fixes #9 'model scale inconsistent between GLTF files')

Together these two fixes are the most direct available explanation for mistakeprompt.md #1 ('large object clipping at top of screen') and #8 ('huge white circle fills most of the screen'): an un-normalized GLB authored at a much larger native scale, combined with the scale-prop-discarding bug above forcing it toward ~1.0x, could plausibly render large enough to enclose the camera or fill the frame near the top of the viewport

Not independently verified by running the dev server / visual QA in this session (filesystem-only access, no execution capability against this project) -- implemented and reviewed by careful reading of the render/animation code paths, but should be spot-checked visually across a range of satellites (especially ones that previously looked most oversized/undersized) before considering this closed

Reviewed the remaining 20 items in mistakeprompt.md against the current codebase: the large majority (previous-model cleanup/accumulation #3/#15/#16/#17, inconsistent left/right/top positioning #6, Chandrayaan/Moon/Mars/Sun camera travel #7, text/model overlap #11, scroll timing #12, camera continuity #14, orbit-line/Earth-clipping #4-partial) already have dedicated fixes from earlier sessions per this changelog and were confirmed still in place in the current source. #5 ('satellite transformation not visually clear -- reads as one model disappearing and another appearing') is a genuine remaining gap: transformation particles exist but there's no true cross-fade/morph between the outgoing and incoming satellite models. changeLog.summary: Scroll-controlled satellite motion plus matching scroll-density treatment for the launch countdown (this chat session)
changes: Converted satellite orbital motion from time-based (clock.elapsedTime, orbited automatically regardless of scrolling) to pure scroll-progress-driven motion: each satellite now sweeps exactly one full orbital revolution across its dedicated SATELLITE_TRANSITION_BAND, is fully reversible, and holds still the instant scrolling stops (JourneyScene.tsx: OrbitingSatellite, new ORBIT_SWEEP and SPIN_RATIO constants)

Raised SATELLITE_TRANSITION_BAND from 0.12 to 0.8 and changed SCROLL_TRACK_HEIGHT from a flat 600vh constant to a value dynamically derived from VH_PER_PROGRESS_UNIT times total journey progress, so one orbital revolution now takes several deliberate scroll actions instead of finishing within a single scroll gesture (constants.ts, page.tsx)

Added feature: applied the same multiple-scroll-actions treatment to the T-05 to LIFTOFF launch countdown, which previously flashed by in under 11vh of scroll. Added COUNTDOWN_SCROLL_WEIGHT (constants.ts) and a new piecewise scroll-to-progress mapping, computeWeightedJourneyLength and progressFromScrollFraction (lib/utils.ts), that gives only the countdown window extra physical-scroll density while leaving every other launch-phase progress boundary unchanged

Swapped JourneyProvider's handleScroll from a flat raw times totalJourneyEnd mapping to progressFromScrollFraction, and page.tsx's SCROLL_TRACK_HEIGHT to computeWeightedJourneyLength, so both the satellite orbit and countdown scroll-pacing fixes flow from these two call sites (JourneyProvider.tsx, page.tsx)

Added feature: full-screen blink/flash effect fired on every T-minus countdown tick (T-05 to LIFTOFF), keyed to the countdown digit itself so it declaratively re-triggers via React remount on each change in either scroll direction, no timers or effects needed. New countdown-blink keyframe and animate-countdown-blink utility class added to the reduced-motion disable list (globals.css); rendered as a fixed full-screen div in JourneyOverlay.tsx. Color tuned from an initial cyan tint to solid black per follow-up feedback

Tuned COUNTDOWN_SCROLL_WEIGHT through several passes based on feel: 8 (initial) to 4 (felt like too much scrolling) to 10 (4 advanced too fast) to 20 (10 still not slow enough) — current value 20 gives roughly 206vh total across the six countdown stages, about 34vh per stage (constants.ts)

SatelliteModel.tsx.description: Loads a dedicated real GLB model per spacecraft (all 23, from public/models/satellites/) with 6 procedural geometry builders (Science, Lander, Orbiter, Comms, Solar, Box) retained as the Suspense fallback while a model loads; includes hover glow, smooth scaling, Html floating label, and pointer click event handler

Earth.tsx.description: 3D Earth with high-res texture maps and custom GLSL atmosphere terminator shader; no cloud layer (removed per explicit request)

SpaceEnvironment.tsx.description: Deep space starfield with GLSL twinkling, procedural canvas nebula clouds, distant galaxies, floating particles, and cinematic lighting

RestartTransition.tsx.description: Cinematic Restart Journey transition — nose-first rocket with trailing flame streaks right-to-left across the screen, fog fades in to fully cover it, journey state resets underneath, fog clears to reveal the Hero screen. JourneyProvider.tsx.description: Unified state management for scroll progress (ref + state), active satellite index tracking, details panel state, and position save/restore

useReducedMotion.ts.description: Detects the OS prefers-reduced-motion media query and returns a boolean; wired into animation toggles (RestartTransition cinematic, countdown flash) for accessibility compliance per section 26

usePerformanceMode.ts.description: Hardware-adaptive tier hook (high/medium/low) scoring device memory, CPU cores, touch capability, and WebGL support; drives quality scaling (particle counts, texture resolution, post-processing) per section 21

useIsMobile.ts.description: Window-resize breakpoint (default 768px) detection hook used to adapt UI and 3D rendering to mobile viewports per section 22

models.generate.description: GET endpoint that procedurally builds demo GLB binary models (ARYABHATA, MANGALYAAN, CHANDRAYAAN-3, ADITYA-L1, and the PSLV launch vehicle) via a pure-Typescript glTF 2.0 binary writer into /public/models/. video.history.description: GET endpoint returning all video-generation jobs sorted by creation date (descending), sourced from lib/videoState.ts

video.status.description: GET endpoint that polls a video job's status from the OpenRouter generations API, maps it to the local status enum, and persists updates via lib/videoState.ts
